diagnostic_evidence.quote: i.e., $\A_j = \U_j\T_j\U_j^*$, with $\U_j$ unitary and $\T_j$ upper triangular

issues.failure_explanation: The asserted orthogonal similarity need not exist on the stated complex domain. For example, A=[[1,i],[i,-1]] is nonzero, symmetric, and satisfies A²=0. An orthogonal similarity UᵀAU would remain symmetric. If also triangular, it would be diagonal and, because both eigenvalues are zero, would vanish, a contradiction. General complex Schur reduction requires unitary bases and adjoints, not the asserted orthogonal bases and transposes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: i.e., $\A_j = \U_j\T_j\U_j^*$, with $\U_j$ unitary and $\T_j$ upper triangular
Observe that we compute the matrix exponentials by means of the Matlab command \verb|expm|.

issues.failure_explanation: The ordinary scalar Parlett recurrence divides by differences of triangular diagonal entries. For T=[[0,1],[0,0]], its first off-diagonal equation is 0·E12=0 and does not determine E12, although exp(tT)=[[1,t],[0,1]]. Such repeated Schur eigenvalues are permitted, and no distinctness hypothesis or block/confluent branch is supplied. This obstruction can occur even when the full Sylvester operator is invertible, for example by taking another coefficient matrix equal to I.

failure_location.quote: and $\exp(t\T_j)$ can be computed efficiently by means of Parlett's algorithm \cite{parlett1976}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain expm for unrestricted inputs. To retain the general native-free alternative, specify block Parlett handling: group equal eigenvalues, evaluate each repeated-eigenvalue block λI+K by its finite nilpotent Taylor formula, and use off-diagonal Sylvester recurrences only between spectrally disjoint blocks.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed exponential fallback for languages without a native exponential routine does not cover all admitted matrices as stated. The MATLAB implementation's separate use of expm is unaffected.
issues.title: The Parlett exponential recommendation omits repeated-eigenvalue handling
issues.why_classification: Covering the omitted case requires a contained block/matrix-function construction, rather than a notation correction. It does not require changing the tensor solver or abandoning the full matrix domain.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: & u_t(\xx, t) = \Delta u(\xx, t) + 2\xx\cdot\nabla u(\xx, t) + (2N+1)u(\xx, t) - \exp(-\xx\cdot\xx), & & \xx\in\mathbb R^N, t > 0,
The solution at $t = 1$, taking $N = 6$ dimensions, took $25.73$ seconds to execute, and the error was $9.6811\times10^{-14}$

issues.failure_explanation: At t=0 the claimed solution equals 2exp(−x·x), whereas the initial datum is exp(−x·x). Writing φ=exp(−x·x), the spatial operator satisfies (Δ+2x·∇+(2N+1))φ=φ. Thus the prescribed Gaussian initial datum gives the stationary solution u=φ; the stated time-dependent expression instead corresponds to initial datum 2φ. Consequently, that expression cannot validate the displayed IVP.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, the solution of \eqref{e:uxt} is $u(\xx, t) = (1+\exp(t))\exp(-\xx\cdot\xx)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the test consistent: either change the initial datum to 2exp(−x·x) to retain the stated time-dependent solution, or use the stationary solution exp(−x·x) for the displayed initial datum. Align the numerical initialization and reference solution, then recompute the reported error.
issues.overall_effect: The exact solution and the reported numerical validation cannot both refer to the stated initial-value problem. The general discretization method is not refuted by this mismatch.
issues.title: The claimed advection-diffusion solution violates the prescribed initial condition
issues.why_classification: Repair requires choosing which mathematical test was intended and revalidating its error, not merely a forced notation correction. A comparable advection-diffusion experiment remains available without changing the general method.
